title: kv-cache: adaptive spillover + eviction-priority + background defrag to reduce fragmentation
author: Priya Natarajan
description:
Motivation: KV cache fragmentation under long-running streams and aggressive prefix caching causes memory pressure and unexpectedly frequent spillovers. This PR introduces a set of coordinated changes to reduce fragmentation, make spillover decisions adaptive to workload, and continue to meet latency SLOs.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds an eviction priority that prefers removing small, highly fragmented entries and cold prefixes before evicting large contiguous KV segments. This reduces fragmentation and avoids multiple small allocations scattered in GPU/host memory.
- Introduces an adaptive spillover threshold: instead of a fixed bytes threshold, we consider active workload signals (sequence length distribution, rate of new keys, resident set fragmentation metric) and allow transient bursts without immediate spillover while enforcing steady-state caps.
- Background defragmentation worker: a low-priority, rate-limited thread that coalesces free regions and optionally migrates cold contiguous segments to a host-backed spillover pool during low utilization windows. The worker respects SLOs (pause on high latency or when GPU load exceeds configured percentage).
- Observability: new metrics for fragmentation_ratio, avg_free_chunk_size, defrag_runs, spillover_adaptive_decisions, and kv_eviction_reason. Dashboards updated in redwood-console to show fragmentation trends per model.
- Scheduling improvements: eviction and defrag tasks are now scheduled through the serving runtime scheduler so they don't contend with token-generation critical paths; continuous-batching paths gain a short-circuit check to avoid cache-side stalls.
- Tests and microbench: unit + integration tests covering eviction ordering and spillover policy, as well as a perf microbenchmark that simulates long-chat workloads. Microbench results: 12–28% reduction in spillover events and 6–10% end-to-end P95 latency improvement for chat workloads with highly variable sequence lengths.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation
- [x] Unit & integration tests
- [x] Perf microbench + numbers in PR description
- [x] Console metric plumbing and dashboard note
- [x] Documentation note in runtime/README (short)

Rationale & design notes:
- The eviction-priority heuristic uses a cost model that scores entries by (fragmentation_penalty * fragment_count + size_penalty * size_bytes - recency_bonus). This is intentionally tunable via runtime_config to allow SRE tuning per workload/class.
- Adaptive spillover avoids oscillation when a short-lived burst would otherwise trigger aggressive spillover and then immediate re-ingest; it uses a leaky-bucket style smoothing of recent allocation rate and a fragmentation-aware headroom.
- Background defrag is conservative: it only merges free blocks that reduce fragmentation_ratio by a configured delta and it can be bumped to more aggressive modes by ops during maintenance windows.

Compatibility & migration:
- Default behavior enabled behind runtime flag kv.defrag.enabled=true and kv.spillover.adaptive=true. We flip the flags for dedicated fleets after validation. The runtime gracefully falls back to previous behavior if the defrag worker cannot acquire memory moves (e.g., in private/airgapped installs without host-spill pool).

Related: ENG-3245 (investigation), ENG-3301 (eviction policy revamp), SUP-1120 (customer report of repeated spillovers).

review_comments: Diego Martinez (2026-02-18): Nice set of changes — can you expand on how the eviction scoring treats very large cold KV segments? We don't want repeated churn on huge keys.

Priya Natarajan (2026-02-18): Reply: eviction score penalizes fragment_count heavily; for very large cold segments size_penalty is reduced by a tunable factor 'size_decay_for_cold' so we tend to prefer evicting many small fragmented entries before a single large contiguous one. Added comment and a unit test for large cold segment behavior.

Liam O'Connor (2026-02-20): Scheduler integration looks good. Two nits: 1) make defrag worker backoff multiplier configurable, 2) ensure the worker yields to high-priority IO tasks.\n\nPriya (2026-02-21): Addressed both: added config and explicit runtime check against scheduler load; also added comment linking to SRE playbook.

Zara Patel (2026-02-22): Observability looks sufficient; can we expose a per-customer fragmentation alert threshold?\n\nPriya (2026-02-23): Added kv_fragmentation_alert_threshold in metrics config and a console note.

release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: adaptive spillover, fragmentation-aware eviction priority, and background defragmentation worker. Reduces spillover events and lowers P95 latency on long-chat workloads. Config flags: kv.defrag.enabled, kv.spillover.adaptive.
